sections.text: Thus, O Mighty-in-Arms, knowing Him to be beyond the intellect and, by His help, subduing thy personal egotism, kill thine enemy, Desire, extremely difficult though it be.

We had been discussing Chapter 3, Karma Yoga, Yoga of Action. In Chapter 2, Bhagavan had given us indication about who we are at the core of our being. That the self that I think I am is not the Self, but my self is imperishable, everlasting, all knowing and ever blissful. And it is contrary to my own experience. So it becomes a hypothesis for me. Its not my knowledge right now that the self is all pervading, everlasting, ever blissful.
My life is completely contrary to that. So Bhagawan says, thats because of your ignorance about yourself. So once I remove that ignorance, then I should be able to know the knowledge. Thats basically our hypothesis right now. But my effort to know that is not very fruitful so far. So we have to accept that there is a limitation for me to know.
Even all Western scholars and philosophers have come to the conclusion that there is a limit for the rational thinking to get knowledge. Immanuel Kant said, I have to limit my reasoning to make room for faith that there is God or there is a Creator of this universe. And you can postulate a theory, but it does not become my knowledge. You have to rely on faith. Our scriptures say you dont really have to rely on just faith, but you can experience that if you follow certain path, then you will be able to know this. In fact, our scripture says it is your birthright to know this knowledge.
And you will know that when not guaranteed. So you have to make efforts. Efforts means activity, and activity as we know, has its own limitation. So in the beginning of this chapter, having been taught by Bhagavan Karmani, Eva di Karaste Mahphale Shukadachana, your right is only to act, never the fruits of actions. And therefore Yogastha kuru Karmani, establish yourself in yoga and then do your actions and you shall come to know this knowledge. But Arjuna obviously was not convinced that this activity is going to get me anywhere.
So obviously he asked that question. If you think then I have to establish Myself in yoga which is basically sit down, meditate and become a yogi. Then why are you asking me to engage in this war which is a terrible act? Why dont you tell me the act and can lead me to a greater understanding? So Bhagavan basically clarifies: Loke Asmin Dvividha Nishtha Pura Prokta Mayanagha -- in this world, two paths are created right from the beginning. Gnana Yogena Sankhyanam Karma Yogena Yoginam -- for people with Sankhya Buddhi, the contemplative intellect, the path is Gnana Yoga. This means contemplating on the fact that I am not this body, I am not this mind, I am not the intellect. Then who am I? is basically Gnana Yoga. And Karma Yogena Yoginam -- those who are active in this life, for them it is Karma Yoga. So basically, Bhagavan transformed Karma into Karma Yoga. And we have seen that Bhagavan has given five pointers.
Two we get in chapter two. You should not have the fruit in your mind as the goal for your action and establishing Yoga. Perform your all actions. Bhagwan says there are two parts. But for you Karma Yoga is good. Where you are in the station of your life, Karma Yoga will be much better.
There are three paths we typically talk about. Karma Yoga, Gnana Yoga and Bhakti Yoga. Karma and Gnana I have control over. At least I can make my efforts in them. Bhakti I can only get by Gods grace. To fall in love is not something in my hand.
When you fall in, there is no choice in love. Bhakti is love for divine and it is choiceless. It only comes by the grace of God. Therefore Bhagawan said, start with Karma Yoga. That Karma Yoga will lead you to knowledge about God. The Bhagavan said, activity is involuntary for all beings.
Na Kaschit Kshanam Api Jatu Tishthaty Akarmakrit -- but you should act in this world by controlling your senses and without any attachment. So Bhagavan said, when Prajapati created this Praja, he also created Yajna at the same time. To sustain this Praja, Yajna was created. So we worry about our children: how would they sustain themselves when we are not there?
So we have to make them independent. How do you make them independent? By this education you shall earn your living. So focus on your education. Thats how we do as parents. Prajapati did something similar -- Prajapati created Yajna, cooperative activity where you work with nature.
This cooperation between the beings in nature will yield results which will sustain this praja. So then we have seen a cycle in this Prakriti Annad Bhavati Bhutani, Prajanyatamna Sambhavah. And in the end says Karma Brahmod Bhav that the unit of this cycle is action. All that is happening in this Prakriti is happening because of activity in the Prakriti. And this activity is only possible at an individual level. At an individual level, if we act, then this activity becomes a communal activity, a national activity, a global activity.
But at an individual level you have to act. Then Bhagavan said, this ability to act comes from that Brahman, the supreme consciousness which is functioning through you. As long as Im alive, I can act. So Bhagavan said, know that this activity is based in your consciousness and therefore you continue activity without any attachment. Because activity is to acquire something I dont have and preserve what I have. But if I come to a conclusion that I have acquired everything I want, should I continue to act?
For the Loka Sangra, for the preservation of the community, of the society, of this universe, you have to continue working. Look, I have nothing to gain, but I continue to work. If I dont act or work, then there will be a chaos in this cosmos. To avoid this chaos, the Sankarasyacha Kartashyam I will become the cause for this chaos in this world and therefore I continue to work. And then he comes to his final advice in verse 30 where he says, Mai Sarvani Karmani Sanyasya Adhyatma Chet Nirasi Nirmama Bhutva yudhiya, you offer all your actions to me. In this one verse, Bhagavan has given us a complete method of Karma Yoga.
Act you must but act in a manner of Karma Yoga. Now what is Karma Yoga? He said, when you act with that attitude that Im offering all my actions to the Supreme Lord. Because we have seen in that natural cycle that acts, activity at my level is only possible because I am a conscious being. That life in me, that consciousness in me is not different than the consciousness which is all pervading. Therefore I should offer all my activities to that supreme consciousness.
Nirasi Nirmama Bhutva -- without any desire for a particular result from my actions. And Nirmama means not thinking anything is mine; even this ability to act is not my own. This ability to act is Gods gift to me. I did not do much to prepare that this type of body. I will have this type of mind, I will have this intellect developer. Well, this was given to me as my instrument and Im now just using them.
If I have better equipment than some other person, its not something that I have done in this life, at least. So Bhagavan said, Nirashi Nirmamo Bhutva -- you become desireless and without any sense of mine. Therefore, you should act according to your own dharma. Wherever you are, whatever station you are at in your life, you should act according to that, because you dont really have any choice but to act according to that. I cant suddenly wake up one morning and say, I really dont want to act as an architect anymore.
You know, this business is not doing well for me. Im going to become something else. Well, I dont really have an ability to change right away. So Bhagavan said, Swadharma Nidhanam, Sreyaha Paradharmo Bhya Vah, you act according to your own dharma, according to your own Prakriti. Because to act like someone else is very dangerous. It may seem easy right now, it may seem glamorous right now, but because it is not your nature, you will fail eventually and you will not make any progress.
So therefore, he said, even a wise person is also bound by his own Prakriti. When a wise person is not free from his own nature, he also acts according to his own nature. Except that he does not consider that as his own nature. He considers this the nature of my body, mind and intellect. I offer all that I do to the Lord who is making me do that. You are bound by the Prakriti because you are part of Prakriti.
Your Prakriti is basically who you are at this point and therefore know your nature and act accordingly. In Arjunas case, he said, you are a Kshatriya. You are a prince who is responsible to protect others. And now you are in front of this enemy army. Your job is to fight this war. In whatever station of life I am in, I should act accordingly.
Prakriti works by likes and dislikes. I have created likes and dislikes by my experiences in the world of objects. Some experiences I like, some I dislike. These likes and dislikes reside in my senses, in my sense perception. Some sense perceptions were pleasurable,
some were painful. They are your obstructions, and therefore avoid them. If that is the case, just tell me: what is the force which makes people commit sins against their own will? Knowing this is not right, I commit that act and then I come to suffer for it. So Bhagavan said, Kama Esha Krodha Esha. In the end, it came down to this: my likes and dislikes are the root cause of how I act.
If I overcome my likes and dislikes then it will be much easier for me to act in a rational manner. Why I have not been able to do that is because of the Kama and Krodha. This likes and dislikes create desire. That desire creates anger. This Kama is the root cause of all my problems. So Bhagavan said, therefore consider them to be your enemies.
This desire and anger are veiling my true nature. We started a journey from I do not know my true self and therefore all my problems in life. If I know my true self, Ill be almighty, all pervading, omniscient, omnipresent. That knowledge has been veiled by this Kama and Krodha. Therefore Bhagavan said Avrutam Gnana Methina. Now this Gnana is the Gnana of myself.
Avruttam Gnanameti na Gnanino Nitya Vairina bhai. This knowledge is veiled from even a wise person. Kama Rupena kaunteya duspuraynanalynacha Kama desire. It is insatiable like a fire. And therefore Bhagavan says, Indriyani Mano Buddhih Asya Adhishthanam Uchyate. To fight the enemy, you have to find his location.
The location of my enemy is Indriyani Manah Buddhi Senses, mind and intellect are this desires residences. I identified where this desire resides. It deludes the embodied by veiling his wisdom. A simple fact Bhagavan said is this desire is veiling your wisdom about your own self. And therefore this desire is your enemy. The desire is residing in your senses first by the sense perception.
This perception creates the conception of that object and then I have desire to acquire that object. If I cant acquire the object of my desire then Im angry. This desire and anger is veiling your true self. And therefore, Tasmat Tvam Indriyany Adau Niyamya Bharatarshabha. Dont let this enemy come into your house. Once it enters your house, you are in trouble.
Therefore you have to lock your doors, have a security system.

The final verse of Chapter 3 is Krishnas battle cry: Jahi shatrum mahaabaaho kaamarupam durasadam - O mighty-armed one, slay this enemy in the form of desire, difficult though it is to conquer! The path is clear: knowing that the Self is beyond the intellect (evam buddheh param buddhva), steady yourself in that Self (samstabhya atmanam atmana), and destroy desire. This is not suppression but transcendence - rising to a level of identity where desire cannot touch you.
The word durasadam (difficult to overcome) is important. Krishna does not promise an easy victory. Desire is indeed a formidable enemy - it has been with us since beginningless time, it operates through our own instruments, it is insatiable and ever-renewing. But mahaabaaho - mighty-armed one - you have the strength for this battle. The strength comes not from willpower but from knowledge and proper positioning. Established in the Self, you are invincible.
As Chapter 3 concludes, take time to integrate its teachings. The chapter began with Arjunas confusion about action versus knowledge, and ends with a call to action - jahi (slay!). The entire arc of Karma Yoga is here: you must act, but act as Yajna; work in the world, but remain established in the Self; engage with the gunas, but know you are beyond them; face your desires, but slay them from the vantage point of your true identity. Today, choose one desire that has been troubling you. Rather than fighting it directly, ask: From where am I fighting? Can I establish myself, even momentarily, in that which is beyond the intellect - my witnessing awareness - and from there see desire as something that arises and passes, unable to touch who I really am? This shift from battleground to observation deck is the essence of victory.
